_comment: The judge instrument is frozen. held_out_guard() refuses held-out scoring unless the prompt, rubric, rubric axes, rendered prompt AND user turn still hash to these values. Freezing is a recorded act: an agreement number computed on the set the judge was tuned against measures nothing (SPEC/03). The top-level digests are the CURRENT instrument; `instruments` records every one that has published a number, so a stranger can tell which instrument produced which figure.
frozen_after: the instrument-A held-out pass (milestones/M03/judge/held-out/). No prompt, rubric or band definition was touched. Instrument B exists because instrument A supplied half of a classification refusal and because the freeze could not see the half it supplied.
tuning: None, and none since the prompt was written. The prompt, the rubric and the bands are byte-identical to instrument A - `prompt_sha256`, `rubric_sha256`, `rubric_axes_sha256` and `rendered_sha256` are unchanged from the 2026-08-20 freeze and can be diffed against it in this file. Only the user turn moved, and it moved for a reason that has nothing to do with what the judge is asked to score.

instruments.published: milestones/M03/judge/held-out-report.json - the first held-out agreement number
instruments.user_turn_note: There was no digest. The template was a Python literal in evals/judge.py and none of the four frozen digests covered it, so `evals.judge.user_turn` could be replaced wholesale and `is_frozen()` still returned True. `user_turn_template` below is that literal, recovered verbatim from b149572, so instrument A stays re-derivable by a stranger. It is recorded as text and NOT hashed into a `user_turn_sha256`: writing a digest here would read as a pin that existed at the time, and the absence of one is the finding.
instruments.tuning: None. The prompt was written once, before the dev pass, and was not edited after. The dev pass yielded four judged case-instances and two borderline disagreements - too little signal to tune against, and tuning toward labels drafted by this same model family is the circularity the 0% correction rate already flagged. Frozen untuned, and that is recorded rather than claimed as rigour.

b_differs_from_a_in: The two opening labels: `VIEWER QUESTION:`/`VIEWER CONTEXT:` become `QUESTION AS ASKED:`/`REQUEST CONTEXT:`. `viewer` is a SUBJECT_TERM in platform/gateway/core/classify.py, so the instrument supplied the subject half of a personal-data classification and the answer under test supplied the attribute half. Across the eight committed agent runs this refused 9 of 169 case-by-answer renderings, on `entitlement-012` and `grounded-019`; instrument B refuses none. tests/test_judge.py pins both halves of that.

One trailing newline. Instrument A's literal ended at `AXES: {axes}`; the template file ends with a newline, and `render_user_turn` returns the template as written rather than stripping it. Recorded because the re-run's delta must be attributable to the whole difference between the instruments and not only to the interesting half - a newline is not expected to move a band, and 'not expected to' is not a measurement.
